terminalArtifact: Draft pull request based on current origin/main, with integration checks and documentation validation recorded.
boundary: Canonical tool settlement retains oversized captured text or JSON, returns a bounded initial view and opaque session reference, and permits authorized exact readback, within-result discovery and confined computation until expiry.
invariants: Retention stores output protected by the secret-output boundary; captured text and JSON sizes are evaluated independently of initial model-view size.
Opaque references authorize nothing by themselves; trusted invocation session scope and current read permission govern every retrieval.
Result storage is immutable, private, integrity checked, bounded and expires after seven days.
Capture loss is disclosed; retained content never claims to recover bytes a producer did not capture.
Result references survive durable-output bounding and history pruning without repeated prompt rewrites.
Computation receives only already-authorized data, runs the restricted interpreter in a terminable worker and cannot call host tools.
Search is bounded lexical discovery within an explicit result; counts and absence claims require exhaustive inspection or computation.
Existing durable execution settlement remains the sole retry boundary; retrieval never re-executes the source tool.

computation.qualification: Allocation and fuel are conservative interpreter budgets, not OS isolation or an RSS guarantee. Node additionally applies worker heap limits; Bun does not enforce that worker option.

knownLimitations: Result discovery scans at most 256 directory entries and explicitly reports incomplete coverage. Exact access by known ID still works beyond that cap.
Unsupported or oversized structured-only captures receive an explicit omission marker; their original structured preview may be unavailable.
The 8 MiB cap bounds each capture envelope; this slice does not add an aggregate disk quota.
Capture cannot recover bytes the source producer omitted. Structured JSON is normalized, while text readback preserves UTF-8 bytes.
Filesystem protections do not defend against an actively hostile process running as the same OS user swapping ancestor directories.
deferrals: Cross-session or child-session sharing requires an explicit authorization design.
Automatic embeddings, recursive model calls, corpus-wide indexing and default compaction-policy changes remain experiments.
Live model quality and billed-token evaluation is separate from local correctness checks.
Merge, release and deployment remain outside the draft pull request terminal condition.
